title: TCM Communication Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the transmission computer (TCM) communication circuit circuit that is lower than it should be. The TCM data line carries data between the transmission computer and the other modules.
symptoms: Transmission may be in limp mode or shift harshly
Other modules may also store communication codes

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the TCM data line circuit
Low battery voltage or poor ground
Failed transmission control module (internal short)
Corroded or water-damaged connector
Faulty control module (rare)

checks: Inspect the TCM data line wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the TCM data line and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the TCM data line.

title: TCM Communication Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the transmission computer (TCM) communication circuit circuit that is higher than it should be. The TCM data line carries data between the transmission computer and the other modules.
symptoms: Transmission may be in limp mode or shift harshly
Other modules may also store communication codes

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the TCM data line circuit
Low battery voltage or poor ground
Failed transmission control module
Wire shorted to another power circuit
Poor ground or loose connector
Faulty control module (rare)

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the TCM data line circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the TCM data line against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the TCM data line.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure
plain: The transmission computer found that hydraulic pressure is not what it should be for the current conditions.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low or dirty transmission fluid
Faulty pressure control solenoid
Faulty fluid pressure sensor
Worn pump or internal leak

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Compare actual and commanded pressure on a scan tool
Do a mechanical line pressure test
fix: Correct the fluid level first, then repair the solenoid, sensor or internal leak that is causing the pressure problem.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Low
plain: The transmission computer sees hydraulic pressure lower than it should be. Low pressure lets clutches slip and can quickly damage the transmission.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low transmission fluid from a leak or under-filling
Clogged transmission filter
Faulty pressure control solenoid
Worn pump or internal leak from seals or valve body
Faulty pressure sensor reading falsely low

checks: Check the fluid level and look for leaks
Do a mechanical line pressure test to confirm low pressure
Check the pressure control solenoid and its wiring
fix: Fix any leak and correct the fluid level, then service the filter; a solenoid or pump repair may be needed if pressure stays low.
drive: Check for leaks and low fluid. If it shifts normally, keep trips short and gentle and get it checked in the next few days.
test_first: Check fluid level and look for leaks, then measure actual line pressure with a gauge and compare it to the sensor reading before replacing the sensor, pump or valve body.
urgent_if: If the transmission slips, is slow to go into gear, runs hot or goes into limp mode, stop driving and have it towed. Low fluid pressure can burn up the clutches quickly.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure High
plain: The transmission computer sees hydraulic pressure that is higher than it should be, which can make shifts harsh.
symptoms: Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Sticking pressure control solenoid
Stuck pressure regulator valve in the valve body
Faulty fluid pressure sensor reading high
Wiring fault to the pressure control solenoid

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Do a mechanical line pressure test to confirm the reading
Check the pressure control solenoid and its wiring
fix: Usually a pressure control solenoid or valve body repair, after confirming the pressure is truly high.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch C, which reports hydraulic pressure (or on some transmissions, the selected gear range) to the transmission computer.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Failed transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch
Broken or damaged wiring to the pressure sensor/switch
Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground
Faulty transmission or engine computer (rare)

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the pressure sensor/switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the pressure sensor/switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the pressure sensor/switch.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch C is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The pressure sensor/switch reports hydraulic pressure (or on some transmissions, the selected gear range) to the transmission computer.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Failing transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch
Low, dirty or burnt transmission fluid
Sticking valve or blocked passage in the valve body
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Compare the pressure sensor/switch reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the pressure sensor/switch.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch C keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector
Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves
Failing transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the pressure sensor/switch only if it fails testing.

symptoms: Transmission may be stuck in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Failed transmission control module
Weak battery, bad battery terminals or charging problem
Broken or damaged wiring to the TCM power feed
Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground
Faulty transmission or engine computer (rare)

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the TCM power feed for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the TCM power feed against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the TCM power feed.

title: TCM Power Input Signal Low
plain: The transmission computer is seeing lower voltage than it needs on its power feed. A weak battery or bad connection is the usual reason.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode)
Slow cranking or other low-voltage warnings

causes.name: Weak or failing battery
Loose or corroded battery terminals or grounds
Blown fuse or bad relay in the TCM power feed
Charging system not keeping the battery up
Damaged wiring or a faulty transmission computer

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Clean and tighten battery terminals and main grounds
Check the TCM fuse and relay and voltage at the module
fix: Usually fixed by replacing a weak battery or cleaning bad connections; clear the code and check that it stays off.
examples: Often set on Chrysler and Dodge vehicles after a weak battery, dead battery or jump start
drive: Often drivable with care to a shop soon, but low voltage to the transmission computer can leave it in one gear and may mean the battery or charging system is failing. If other warnings appear, it cranks slowly or lights dim, it could stall or not restart, so go straight to a shop.
test_first: Test the battery and charging system, then check the transmission computer's power feed, fuses, relay and ground connections for voltage drop before replacing the module.

title: Transmission Filter Deteriorated
plain: The computer estimates that the transmission filter is getting clogged and should be serviced soon.
symptoms: Check engine or service light on
Usually no change in how the car drives yet

causes.name: Transmission filter due for service
Fluid and filter service done but the computer counter not reset
Heavy towing or hot running wearing the fluid faster

checks: Check service records for the last fluid and filter change
Reset the filter life counter with a scan tool after service
fix: Service the transmission fluid and filter, then reset the filter monitor.

title: Transmission Filter Very Deteriorated
plain: The computer estimates that the transmission filter is badly clogged and needs to be serviced now.
symptoms: Check engine or service light on
Shifts may become slow or harsh

causes.name: Transmission filter well past its service interval
Fluid and filter service done but the computer counter not reset
Debris from internal wear loading up the filter

checks: Check service records for the last fluid and filter change
Look for metal or clutch material in the pan during service
fix: Service the transmission fluid and filter promptly, then reset the filter monitor.

title: Multiple Gears Engaged
plain: The transmission computer sees signs that more than one gear is engaged at the same time. This can lock up or jerk the drivetrain.
symptoms: Sudden jerk, bind or slowdown while driving
Transmission warning or check engine light on
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Sticking shift solenoid or valve in the valve body
Low or contaminated transmission fluid
Clutch pack not releasing inside the transmission
Faulty speed sensor giving false readings

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Scan for solenoid and speed sensor codes
Check gear ratio data on a scan tool during a road test
fix: Often a valve body or solenoid repair; internal clutch damage may need a rebuild.
drive: No. Two gears engaged at once can bind or jerk the drivetrain, which may cause a sudden slowdown or loss of control. If it happened while driving, pull over safely and have it towed. Don't keep driving to see if it happens again.
test_first: Read all transmission codes, check fluid level and condition, and test shift solenoids, valve body operation and speed sensor data before deciding on internal repair.

title: Transmission Component Slipping
plain: The computer compares engine and transmission speeds and sees that something inside the transmission is slipping when it should be locked up.
symptoms: Engine revs rise without the car speeding up
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low or worn-out transmission fluid
Worn clutch packs or bands inside the transmission
Faulty shift or pressure control solenoid
Torque converter problem
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check the fluid level and condition (burnt smell, debris)
Scan for solenoid codes and check for software updates
Watch input and output speeds on a scan tool during a road test
fix: Check fluid and solenoids first; if parts inside are worn, the transmission needs a rebuild or replacement.
drive: Drive as little as possible. If the engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the transmission is slipping, which builds heat and wears clutches fast. Avoid highways and towing, and if it slips badly, smells burnt or goes into limp mode, have it towed.
test_first: Check fluid level, color and smell, read any solenoid or sensor codes, and check line pressure and speed sensor data before deciding the transmission needs a rebuild.

title: Shift Time Too Short
plain: A gear change happened faster than the computer expected, which often feels like a harsh or banging shift.

causes.name: Pressure control solenoid problem causing high pressure
Transmission adaptive values need a reset or relearn
Wrong or worn transmission fluid
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check fluid level and type
Check for software updates or service bulletins
Reset transmission adaptives and road test
fix: Check fluid and updates, relearn the transmission, then repair the pressure control if harsh shifts continue.

title: Shift Time Too Long
plain: A gear change took longer than the computer expected, which can feel like a slip or flare between gears.

causes.name: Low or worn-out transmission fluid
Pressure control or shift solenoid problem
Worn clutch packs inside the transmission
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Scan for solenoid codes
Check for software updates or service bulletins
fix: Correct the fluid and check for updates first; solenoid or internal repair may be needed.

title: Transmission Fluid Deteriorated
plain: The transmission computer estimates that the fluid has broken down from age or heat and needs to be changed.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Shifts may feel rough or slow
Fluid may look dark or smell burnt

causes.name: Transmission fluid past its service life
Overheating from towing or heavy loads
Fluid changed but the fluid life counter not reset

checks: Check the fluid color and smell
Check service records and reset the fluid life counter after service
fix: Change the transmission fluid (and filter if fitted), then reset the fluid life monitor.

title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
plain: The circuit the transmission computer uses to request the check engine light has a voltage that is too low, often from a wire shorted to ground.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Request wire shorted to ground
Corroded connector at the transmission computer
Faulty transmission or engine computer

checks: Check the transmission computer for its own stored codes
Check the request wire for a short to ground
fix: Repair the shorted wire or connector; replace a module only after the wiring tests good.

title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit High
plain: The circuit the transmission computer uses to request the check engine light has a voltage that is too high, often from an open wire or short to power.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Request wire open or shorted to voltage
Loose connector at either module
Faulty transmission or engine computer

checks: Check the transmission computer for its own stored codes
Check the request wire for an open or a short to voltage
fix: Repair the faulty wire or connector; replace a module only after the wiring tests good.
